parties: Sushil Kumar Aggarwal acquirer; AVRO INDIA LIMITED (NSE-listed target)
headline: Sushil Kumar Aggarwal files substantial acquisition disclosure for AVRO INDIA LIMITED under SEBI Reg 31(4)
sum: Material acquisition trigger: Sushil Kumar Aggarwal has submitted a Regulation 31(4) substantial acquisition disclosure to NSE for AVRO INDIA LIMITED, mandating takeover notification under SEBI's 2011 regime. The filing indicates a crossing of statutory share/voting/control thresholds requiring public transparency.
implication: Substantial acquisition filings under Reg 31(4) lock mandatory takeover conditions (open offer, minimum price benchmarking, creeping acquisition rules) if control intent is signalled—even at preliminary disclosure stage the acquirer's subsequent conduct is subject to SEBI scrutiny and can trigger open offer obligations.
detail: Sushil Kumar Aggarwal has made a formal disclosure under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4), which requires notification whenever a person acquires shares, voting rights or convertible securities resulting in a crossing of statutory thresholds (typically 25%, 35%, 55%, 75% bands) or accruing control. The disclosure was filed with the NSE in relation to AVRO INDIA LIMITED, a listed entity. The specific stake percentage, acquisition consideration, timing and stated intent (control acquisition vs. investment holding) are detailed in the formal disclosure document maintained in NSE archives. This is a material corporate governance event requiring mandatory public disclosure and triggering ongoing regulatory obligations.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandates disclosure when a person acquires shares/voting rights/convertible securities crossing statutory thresholds or accruing control; triggers takeover code compliance.
Defines 'acquirer', 'control' and exemptions; critical for determining whether Reg 31(4) trigger applies and what subsequent obligations follow.
If acquirer crossed 25% threshold or signalled control intent, open offer to public shareholders becomes mandatory; minimum pricing rules apply.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011, Regulation 10 (Creeping Acquisition Exemption)
framework.note: 5% annual limit on acquisitions for listed acquirers absent open offer; Reg 31(4) disclosure may lock this exemption depending on declared intent.
If open offer triggered, acquirer must offer at least 90th percentile price of prior 26-week weighted average or highest price paid in prior 52 weeks.
Grants SEBI power to make takeover regulations; provides statutory backbone for enforceability of disclosure and acquisition rules.
Acquirers intending to appoint directors must comply with appointment and disclosure rules; often intersects with takeover filings.
Listing agreement and continuous disclosure obligations; NSE may impose additional requirements on acquirers and target management.

conditions: Crossing of statutory threshold for substantial acquisition (share %, voting rights or control accrual)
Compliance with Regulation 31(4) disclosure format and timing requirements
If control intent signalled or 25%+ threshold crossed, potential mandatory open offer to public shareholders
approvals: SEBI/NSE formal receipt and acceptance of Regulation 31(4) disclosure
Potential SEBI approval/clearance if any exemptions sought from open offer or creeping acquisition rules
Target company board notification and disclosure to stock exchanges
structure.novel: Standard SEBI takeover threshold crossing; no novel structuring indicated in disclosed filing.

triggers.note: Disclosure obligation triggered by acquisition crossing statutory thresholds; initiates mandatory takeover code chain.
If stake ≥25% or control intent declared, open offer becomes mandatory; pricing floor is benchmarked to historical trading.
Acquirer may lose 5% annual creeping exemption once Reg 31(4) disclosure filed, depending on intention statement and stake.
Listed target must immediately notify exchanges and public of material acquisition; failure to disclose or delayed disclosure attracts NSE action.
